function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity itself isn’t “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since antiquity (e.g., static electricity observed by Thales of Miletus). The systematic scientific study of electricity began in the 17th–18th centuries with figures such as William Gilbert (who coined the term “electricus”), Benjamin Franklin (his kite experiment), and Alessandro Volta (inventor of the voltaic pile). Subsequent work by scientists like Luigi Galvani, Michael Faraday, and James Clerk Maxwell built the foundations of modern electrical science.
